model: Residual income on tangible common equity, discounted at cost of equity, with exit P/TBV terminal (bank model)

valuation_philosophy.summary: Citigroup is a G-SIB bank holding company. Free cash flow is not a meaningful valuation concept for a depository/markets institution: deposits and short-term borrowings are operating funding, not net debt; loan origination and trading-book flows swamp any FCF proxy; and regulatory capital (CET1) constrains distributable cash independent of GAAP earnings or OCF. The correct framework is a residual-income (excess-return) model on tangible common equity (TCE), discounted at the cost of equity: intrinsic equity value = starting TCE + PV of future residual income (RI = ROTCE x beginning TCE, minus Cost-of-Equity x beginning TCE) + PV of a terminal exit value based on an assumed exit Price/Tangible-Book-Value multiple, in place of a Gordon-growth FCF terminal value. This directly captures Citi's core investment thesis: after a decade of sub-peer returns (ROE averaged ~5-9% over FY2015-FY2025, well under any reasonable ~10-12% cost of equity), the multi-year Transformation program is largely complete (OCC consent order terminated Dec-2025) and RoTCE has inflected sharply higher -- 13.0-13.1% in Q1/Q2 2026 versus 10-11% full-year guidance and versus mid-single-digit-to-high-single-digit actuals in FY2022-FY2024. The valuation question is whether that inflection is durable (bull), merely a return to the top of guidance (base), or a cyclical Markets/Banking-driven blip that fades back toward the historical sub-scale-consumer-franchise ceiling (bear). A large ongoing buyback ($30B multi-year authorization, ~$13B executed FY2025, ~$10.3B in H1 2026 alone) is modeled as capital-neutral at book (repurchases executed at tangible book value per share, per the standard residual-income convention -- see 'Buyback treatment' below) so that all value creation/destruction flows through the residual-income and exit-multiple terms, not through an assumed buyback discount/premium to book.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_owner_fcf: Reported operating cash flow has been negative in 5 of the last 6 fiscal years shown in the metrics history (FY2019 -$12.8bn, FY2020 -$23.5bn, FY2023 -$73.4bn, FY2024 -$19.7bn, FY2025 -$67.6bn) purely because loan growth, trading inventory and repo/reverse-repo balances are classified as operating activities for a bank -- this is normal and says nothing about intrinsic value. 'Capex' in the metrics CSV is premises-and-equipment spend, immaterial to the economics. Net debt is undefined for an entity whose liabilities are ~$1.6 trillion of deposits, trading liabilities and short-term borrowings that fund earning assets, not leverage on an operating business.
valuation_philosophy.buyback_treatment: Each scenario's buybacks are modeled as repurchases executed at the then-current tangible book value per share (not at a market premium/discount), consistent with the SRBK/NAB precedent in this framework. This is a simplifying convention, not a forecast that Citi will literally buy back stock exactly at TBVPS (the stock currently trades near 1.26x TBVPS) -- its effect is to keep all scenario dispersion attributable to the ROTCE path, the cost of equity, and the terminal exit multiple, rather than to an assumed buyback-price assumption that would otherwise double-count value already captured in the exit multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: RoTCE durability: Q1-Q2 2026's 13%+ RoTCE reflects a decade-best Markets/Banking cyclical upswing (Q2 2026 revenue +14% YoY, 'best quarterly revenue in a decade') layered on top of Transformation-cost runoff; if capital markets activity normalizes lower, RoTCE could revert toward the 10-11% guided range or below

Capital return sustainability: CET1 buffer is ~120bps above the 11.6% regulatory minimum (~12.8% reported) and is being drawn down by an aggressive $30B buyback plus a 12% dividend increase; a credit shock, macro downturn, or Fed SCB/stress-test increase could force a pullback in buybacks, which are a first-order per-share value driver in this model

Banamex divestiture timing/price: the remaining stake sale and eventual IPO are subject to Mexican regulatory approval and market conditions; delay or a weak IPO valuation prolongs capital drag versus what is assumed here
Residual regulatory/Transformation overhang: OCC order terminated Dec-2025, but Federal Reserve commitments continue; a new enforcement action or finding could reintroduce cost or growth restrictions
Card-partnership concentration (Costco, American Airlines) and consumer credit normalization risk to the USPB/USCC segment

Tangible book value per share is ESTIMATED for the current (Q2/Q3 2026) anchor -- see inputs.notes; the CSV's extracted data ends at Q3 2025/FY2025 and no 2026 10-Qs have been parsed into core_metrics yet. The anchor uses FY2025 actuals rolled forward with H1 2026 figures disclosed in the qualitative Analysis (net income, buybacks, dividend), not a fresh balance sheet extraction. Refresh this DCF once Q2/Q3 2026 10-Qs are extracted into the Metrics CSV.

inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 actual (FY2025 10-K, via C_Metrics.csv), rolled forward to an estimated 2026-06-30 position -- see notes
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 actual (1,873.1m per FY2025 10-K), rolled forward to an estimated ~1,785.8m at 2026-06-30
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity (not a blended WACC -- deposits/trading liabilities are the bank's operating funding, not a project financed by debt+equity). Base case 11.0%: US risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST, Sep-2026) + ~6.8pp equity risk premium appropriate to a G-SIB with residual regulatory/EM exposure; consistent with the 9.5-12% range used for SRBK (small thrift) and NAB (AA-rated Australian major bank, 9.7%) in this folder -- Citi sits above NAB (more complex, lower-rated, more cyclical revenue mix, Banamex/EM exposure) and below a distressed thrift.
inputs.lease_treatment: not applicable -- bank model, no lease-adjusted owner FCF
inputs.nci_treatment: immaterial; Citi's minority interests are small relative to total equity and are not separately adjusted for in this model
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank holding company -> residual income on tangible common equity at cost of equity, exit P/TBV terminal (per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing table: 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' -> Residual income on tangible book). NOT an owner-FCF DCF -- deposits are not net debt, and reported OCF/FCF are structurally negative/volatile from balance-sheet growth, not distress (FY2023 OCF -$73.4bn, FY2025 OCF -$67.6bn per C_Metrics.csv). ANCHOR CONSTRUCTION: C_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL) is fully populated only through FY2025/Q3-2025 -- no 2026 10-Q has been extracted into core_metrics yet. To avoid valuing Citi off a 9-month-stale balance sheet, the starting tangible book value and share count are ESTIMATED by rolling the FY2025 actuals (equity $213,822m, shares 1,873.1m, both from the CSV) forward through H1 2026 using figures disclosed in C_Analysis.json's qualitative research: Q2 2026 net income $5.8bn (actual, per company release), Q1 2026 net income estimated at ~$5.34bn (extrapolated at a growth rate consistent with the disclosed 14% YoY revenue growth and RoTCE trend, since Q1 2026 NI was not separately disclosed in the Analysis JSON), H1 2026 buybacks $10.3bn (actual, disclosed), and dividends estimated at the pre-hike $0.56-0.60/quarter rate (the 12% increase to $0.67/share applies from Q3 2026 onward per guidance, not H1). Goodwill + identifiable intangibles are estimated at a constant $22,459m (goodwill ~$18.06bn + intangibles ~$4.4bn), based on the level Citi has carried for several years following the international consumer-exit/Banamex-related write-downs; this is not extracted from a current filing and should be refreshed against the next 10-Q's actual goodwill/intangibles footnote. This estimation chain is a material limitation flagged for the reader: refresh this DCF once Q2/Q3 2026 10-Qs are extracted into C_Metrics.csv, at which point the anchor should be replaced with actuals rather than the rollforward used here.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable to this model -- SBC is embedded in compensation expense feeding net income/ROTCE; no separate owner-FCF SBC add-back is used in a residual-income model
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 actual buybacks per kpis table (C.duckdb); H1 2026 buybacks of $10.3bn disclosed qualitatively in C_Analysis.json are used for the anchor rollforward, not this field

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Standard CAGR growth-rate selection does not apply to a bank residual-income model. Shareholders' equity CAGR is nearly flat (1.3-1.9% over 3-5yr) because large buybacks roughly offset retained earnings -- this is a capital-return story, not a growth story, and per-share value is created primarily through (a) shrinking the share count and (b) ROTCE recovering toward/above cost of equity, not through balance-sheet growth. EPS CAGR is volatile and not a clean anchor either: FY2023 EPS ($4.07) was depressed by elevated expenses/reserve builds and FY2021 EPS ($10.21) was inflated by reserve releases post-COVID, so the reported 5yr EPS CAGR of 8.45% overstates a clean trend. Net-income-based ROTCE trajectory (rising from ~5-8% in FY2022-2025 to a disclosed 13.0-13.1% in H1 2026) is the operative signal driving this valuation, not any revenue or EPS CAGR.

base.narrative: RoTCE glides from 11.5% (just above the top of FY2026 guidance of 10-11%, consistent with management's own commentary of finishing 'a little bit better than the top end') to 13.0% by Y5, i.e. holding the H1 2026 run-rate rather than assuming further acceleration -- Transformation-program completion (~90% of programs at target state, OCC consent order terminated) supports the higher plateau but Markets/Banking cyclicality is assumed to normalize down from the Q2 2026 decade-best print rather than keep accelerating. Buybacks continue at a substantial ~3-4%/year pace (consistent with the $30B authorization and ~$13-20B/year run-rate implied by 2025-2026 actuals), decelerating slightly as the CET1 buffer normalizes. Dividend payout ratio of 35% reflects the $0.67/quarter rate (12% FY2026 hike) against a rising earnings base. Exit at 1.15x tangible book -- modestly above the ~1.0x a sub-cost-of-equity bank would earn, reflecting a RoTCE now running near/at cost of equity, but below where a demonstrably above-cost-of-equity franchise (JPMorgan/BofA trade 2x+ TBV) would be valued, since Citi's Services/Wealth mix-shift story is still maturing and the sub-scale US consumer franchise remains a structural discount versus top-tier peers.

bull.narrative: The H1 2026 RoTCE inflection (13.0-13.1%) proves durable and keeps compounding: Transformation-cost runoff, continued Services/TTS share gains (~120bps/year), a maturing Wealth franchise post the U.S. Retail Banking integration, and a full Banamex exit (freeing capital from a historically low-return business) push RoTCE to 16% by Y5 -- approaching top-tier peer levels. Faster buybacks (4-5%/year, funded by the freed Banamex capital and continued excess CET1) accelerate per-share compounding. Lower cost of equity (10.0%) reflects reduced execution/regulatory risk once the consent-order overhang and Banamex exit are fully behind the company. Exit at 1.4x tangible book, still below JPMorgan/BofA's 2x+ multiples but a re-rating consistent with the market according Citi a 'clean turnaround' premium.

bear.narrative: Q1-Q2 2026's 13%+ RoTCE was a cyclical Markets/Banking-driven blip on a decade-best capital-markets backdrop; as trading volumes and deal flow normalize lower, RoTCE reverts toward the historical FY2022-2025 average (~5-8%) plus only a modest structural uplift from Transformation-cost savings, settling near 9-9.5% -- below the FY2026 guided 10-11% floor. A credit-cycle turn or macro slowdown pressures USPB/USCC card losses and Markets/Banking revenue simultaneously; management responds by conserving capital (buybacks decelerate to ~2%/year, regulatory stress-test outcomes less favorable, CET1 buffer needs rebuilding) and raising the dividend payout ratio (40%) as a smaller, more defensible capital return given lower earnings. New Federal Reserve findings on residual Transformation commitments add cost/uncertainty. Exit at a discount to tangible book (0.9x), consistent with a bank whose ROTCE remains persistently below its cost of equity and whose sub-scale US consumer/wealth franchise keeps it a perennial 'value trap' versus JPMorgan/BofA.

scenario_narratives.base: RoTCE holds the H1 2026 run-rate (~11.5% to 13.0% over 5 years) rather than extrapolating further improvement; buybacks continue at $13-20bn/year pace; exit at 1.15x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Transformation completion + Banamex exit + Services/Wealth share gains push RoTCE to 16% by Y5, a top-tier-adjacent outcome; faster buybacks; exit at 1.4x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2026's RoTCE strength was a capital-markets cyclical peak; reverts to the historical 9-9.5% band as trading normalizes and credit costs rise; buybacks slow; exit at 0.9x (below) tangible book.

base.note: Entry price for a 15% annualized CAGR to the base-case Y5 terminal (exit) value of $182.67/share, which itself embeds a 1.15x exit P/TBV on ~$158.84 ending TBVPS -- i.e. the entry price assumes the RoTCE-recovery and buyback story plays out roughly as modeled in base case, priced back at a 15% hurdle.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = Cost of Equity (CoE), Columns = Exit Price/Tangible-Book-Value multiple (in place of terminal growth rate for a bank residual-income model). Matrix computed on BASE-case RoTCE/buyback/dividend path over 5 years, varying only CoE and exit multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Bear held at the default weight (not reduced) because Citi's balance sheet carries genuine capital-return-sustainability risk (CET1 buffer being actively drawn down by an aggressive $30B buyback + 12% dividend hike) and because the bull and base cases both extrapolate a very recent (2-quarter) RoTCE inflection that has not yet been tested through a full cycle -- a reversion to the historical 5-9% ROTCE band is a live possibility, not a tail case. Bull held at the default weight given the RoTCE trend is real and disclosed by management as durable (not one-off), but is not yet given extra weight given the short observation window.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: current_price sits 63.2% of the way from bear IV ($88.19) to bull IV ($161.14); house and street values coincide in this model because there is no separate SBC-non-cash adjustment (net income already reflects compensation expense as reported) -- band_position is therefore reported as a position within the bear-bull range, not a house-vs-street band.
